column1: # Mario Kart World (Switch 2), the build of the dump the user supplies (SDK 19.3.3, no control data, so no display version): one Application content (version 0), no separate update. In bring-up
# Nintendo EPD's engine (sead / agl / gsys, Phive, Havok 2023.2), SDK 19.3.3 built for the Switch 2 (spec Ounce), NVN2; modules main + subsdk0 (nn::ecli, Nintendo's embedded Mono runtime; main
# imports its allocator) + sdk. This build has no movie module: the 1.8.0 build (SDK 21.4.0: main d00e4f39..., subsdk0 = NintendoSDK movie 746302f4..., subsdk1 = ecli 8dec9c0b..., sdk 7a68b13d...) is
# not registered any more (README, Builds): its dump is not on this machine and a profile has one build row a version and one module list.
# Packed from a dump folder (base/). Shaders: Shader/*.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.bfsha.zs (BNSH with Ampere code), as Donkey Kong Bananza.
# The dump is version 0 as the 1.8.0 one was, so this build takes the v0 row. Its display version is not known (no control.nacp in the dump): the row says "unknown"
# The NPDM declares 64 MB of system resource (virtual address memory on; 1.8.0's NPDM differs only by the services chat:u, mnpp:app and stpl:u). nninitStartup sets the heap to the
# free application memory less a fixed reserve (main+0x84790: 0x5dc00000 in 1.8.0, 0x60400000 in the earlier base build, whose Mac heap check measured 0x1dbc00000): 0x1de400000
# (7.47 GB) in 1.8.0, by that formula (not measured), within the 7.75 GB heap region.
# The alias region holds the SDK's AddressRegionManager node area (0x3fe00000) and then the regions the game maps physical memory into (earlier base build: main+0x68524c), past +1.6 GB within 8 s
# of boot (DM_REGIONS, Switch-sized DM_ALIAS_SIZE); with a 1 GB alias region the first ones got no address and the game read a null object (main+0xc10170). 4 GB: the node area
# and the 1.57 GB (1.53 GB in 1.8.0) the 9 GB pool leaves beside the heap, with room for fragmentation. The Switch 2's 9 GB pool (as Donkey Kong Bananza; not measured)
# The window size is not this game's lever in the profile: main+0xc10190 (movz w21,#1440, in the function at main+0xc0ff60 that fills the renderer's size table) caps the twelve
# heights GamePerformanceGraphicsConfigGParam gives, and a window_fn row naming it ("-", that offset, 2560x1440) was measured to work (the game note, Window size), but game.py allows one
# lever for Game resolution and the profile uses the Switch 2 graphics scale below (measured on the phone on main)
# agl's render buffer binding: Donkey Kong Bananza's clears are wrapped in render conditions; the same engine, not yet checked on this game
# The 3D scenes' size follows the operation mode and the Switch 2 graphics scale, not the window (README, Render resolution): the Android launcher's Game resolution
# sets these instead of DM_WINDOW_SIZE. <choice> <DM_GRAPHICS_SCALE> <operation mode>: handheld scale 0 crops 1920x1080, handheld scale 2 1280x720 (phone rH0 / rH2);
# Original has no row: the game's own (console, scale 1: 2048x1152)
